inputs.proposal: J2534 request modes: the set scheduler owns requests whenever the profile has mux defs, ?poll= is rejected at parse time unless ?filter= gives it a channel, and the single-PID poll request is built on the first channel.
inputs.original_proposal: J2534 request modes: the set scheduler owns requests whenever the profile has mux defs, ?poll= is rejected at parse time unless ?filter= gives it a channel, and the single-PID poll request is built on the first channel.

blockers: claim: C ABI integrity violation: scheduler mode logic incorrectly handles poll_pid, creating ambiguous request ownership between poll and scheduled modes; file: core/src/j2534_transport.cpp; quote: const bool sched_mode = (t->sched.count > 0);

claim: Buffer size assumption violation: hardcoded 8-byte CAN buffer (req[6]) assumes CAN 2.0B format, ignoring CAN-FD support which requires 64+ byte buffers; file: core/src/j2534_transport.cpp; quote: uint8_t req[6];

claim: Thread safety violation: scheduler count accessed without synchronization in worker thread context; sched_mode derived from shared state without mutex protection; file: core/src/j2534_transport.cpp; quote: const bool sched_mode = (t->sched.count > 0);

claim: Memory lifetime violation: hardcoded channel index 0 creates potential use-after-free if chans array is modified or destroyed during channel resolution; file: core/src/j2534_transport.cpp; quote: build_mode01_request(req, t->chans[0].tx_id, t->poll_pid);
questions: How does the scheduler ownership transition work when poll_pid is set vs when sched_mode is true? The change removes the poll_pid check from sched_mode determination.
What synchronization mechanism protects t->sched.count across the attach and worker thread boundaries?
Is there CAN-FD support for 64-byte frames, or is this intentionally CAN 2.0B only?
How is the chans array lifetime managed to prevent the hardcoded index 0 from becoming stale?
nits: Consider adding an assertion that validates channel count > 0 before accessing chans[0]
The error code QT_ERR_NO_TRANSPORT for poll without filter could be more specific (e.g., QT_ERR_INVALID_CHANNEL)
Comment on line 372 could clarify the new scheduler ownership semantics with poll_pid
